title: Tokens are pieces of text
summary: A token is a piece of text used by a model. Tokens can be words, word parts or other pieces. Splitting on spaces is only a teaching shortcut.
introduction: A token is a piece of text used by a model. Tokens can be words, word parts or other pieces. Splitting on spaces is only a teaching shortcut. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain tokens are pieces of text
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A token is a piece of text used by a model. Tokens can be words, word parts or other pieces. Splitting on spaces is only a teaching shortcut.

blocks.code:
text = "The red kite flies"
toy_tokens = text.split()
print(toy_tokens)
blocks.title: Tokens are pieces of text

blocks.text: The output is ['The', 'red', 'kite', 'flies']. split cuts this text at whitespace. Real model tokenizers may split the same sentence differently.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Try a word with punctuation and describe this shortcut's limit.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not use word counts as exact token counts for a real model.
For more detail later, use this [Large Language Models further reading](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1).
